candidates.label: A 王道16bit
candidates.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: visual direction concept art for FantasyRoyale, an original top-down 2D fantasy adventure / party battle royale game.
Create one beautifully finished landscape gameplay-view concept, landscape 3:2 composition. This is an art direction candidate for comparison, not a sprite atlas. Camera is fixed near-overhead orthographic top-down with a slight three-quarter view so the fronts of tree trunks, cliffs, and architecture can be seen. No horizon, no sky, no cinematic perspective. Make it look like a plausible playable 2D game scene with hard-edged pixel art.
Scene motif used in all three candidates: a woodland crossroads clearing; a winding dirt path and small mossy cobblestone plaza; layered tree canopies forming forest edges, visible trunks and roots; an irregular turquoise stream/pond with a short timber footbridge; a low grass-topped rocky ledge; a small rustic merchant shelter with an awning and a few goods near the path; a stone healing spring as a small landmark; mushrooms, ferns, flowers, stumps and rocks placed as meaningful clusters. Keep the center spacious enough for movement and combat, ground detail quieter than props, 3-4 legible exits, passage widths adequate for small characters. It is a local location, not a whole world map.
Include one small provisional adventurer sprite in the clearing, with a simple warm ochre cloak, muted blue clothing, a sword and small shield. Character should occupy about 4 percent of image height and read instantly through silhouette and value contrast. Character design is just for scale, environment remains the main subject.
Draw all terrain transitions with organic stepped contours: irregular grass edges around paths, shallow banks and ripples at water, explicit ledge faces and grounding shadows. Suggest modular 32x32 tile-scale material clusters, but no visible grid. Clear silhouette, restrained ground noise, intentional pixel clusters, highlights and midtones, consistent light from upper left.
No text, no labels, no logo, no watermark, no HUD, no frame, no collage, no sheet, no photorealism, no 3D render, no blur or depth of field, no smooth airbrushed painting. Original design without copying an existing game.
Direction A — CLASSIC VIBRANT ADVENTURE: bright, richly colored GBA-era 16-bit fantasy pixel art. Clean but richly layered leaves with many small crisp clusters, vivid yellow-green grass contrasted with deep emerald forest shadow, turquoise water, warm ochre dirt, earthy brown trunks, weathered grey cobbles. Moderate outline weight, compact angular old-world shelter, blocky stone spring, a sense of summer sunlight and lively adventure. Detail should be plentiful around forest borders and sparse in fighting space. Polished manual pixel-art finish, chunky visible pixels, coherent value grouping. The scene is welcoming and energetic.

refinements.label: A 粗いドット版 v002

refinements.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: FantasyRoyale art-direction refinement, candidate A v002.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the supplied A classic forest adventure concept.
Primary request: keep candidate A's bright adventurous look but make the pixel art a little coarser, with clearly larger and simpler pixel clusters and less tiny detail.
Preserve: the same landscape composition and camera, all main landmark positions and sizes, branching open clearing, winding dirt path and cobbles, left turquoise stream and wooden bridge, tree masses and grass-topped cliffs, upper-right merchant awning, right stone healing spring, center small ochre-cloaked blue-clothed adventurer. Preserve yellow-green / emerald / turquoise / warm earth palette, upper-left lighting and clear movement space.
Redraw the whole scene deliberately as authentic crisp low-resolution 16-bit game art: think a virtual 384x256 canvas enlarged to 1536x1024 with hard square nearest-neighbor pixels. Edges, material strokes and highlights should be visibly stepped and chunkier than the reference. Group many tiny leaf strokes into fewer larger leaf clumps; group stone speckles and grass noise into intentional broader clusters. Simplify the merchant wares and ornament, cobble cracks, woodgrain, flower centers and water ripple count; keep recognizable silhouettes. Use compact coherent tone ramps with distinct dark, midtone and highlight groups. Moderate simplification, still rich attractive fantasy pixel art, not extremely crude 8-bit. Grass must retain purposeful small tufts and variation, with quieter center, never large empty single-color surfaces.
Important: this is a new coarser redraw, not just a blurred filter or unedited copy. The difference must be plainly visible at the full-scene scale while preserving scene identity. No new props, characters or landmarks. No shift towards pastel storybook, no dark mystical variant, no visual grime or distress; 'coarser' means larger pixel clusters and simpler drawing.
Output: one full landscape image, same 3:2 framing, full opaque background. No labels, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no UI, no border, no inset, no collage. No antialiasing, no smooth painterly gradients, no blur, no depth of field.

refinements.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: FantasyRoyale art direction refinement A v003, whole-world deformed/chibi pixel-art concept.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: A's coarser forest crossroads scene.
Primary request: further reduce the adventurer's head-to-body proportions and deform the entire fantasy world to match. This must be a clear whole-world redesign in proportions, not just a larger head pasted on the existing detailed environment.
Preserve the lively original A palette: vivid yellow-green and deep emerald forest, saturated turquoise water, warm ochre dirt, earthy timber, cool grey stones, bright upper-left sunlight. Preserve the scene's overall geography: open central branching clearing, winding left stream and timber bridge, upper-right merchant shelter, right healing spring, tree-bordered paths and grass-topped ledges. Same 3:2 landscape framing, gameplay-oriented top-down near-overhead 2D view with fronts of props visible, no horizon or sky.
Character: one clearly visible small chibi adventurer in the center, about TWO HEADS TALL, head roughly half the entire figure height, squat short torso, short stubby legs, simple mitt-like hands, expressive readable face. Ochre cape, blue outfit, compact sword and round shield remain. Entire character occupies around 6 percent of the scene height, so it reads a little stronger than the reference but still belongs in the game world. Keep chibi proportions visible at game scale. No tall slender anatomy, tiny adult head, elongated limbs, or realistic anatomy.
Entire world deformation:
- Trees: large round lobed canopy silhouettes with just a few broad interlocking leaf masses, thick short trunks and simplified big roots; squat and exaggerated rather than tall intricate realistic trees.
- Rocks and cliffs: large softly rounded chunky boulders and broad simple ledge faces, fewer larger stone facets, simplified grass fringes. Keep gameplay barriers legible.
- Merchant shelter: a small squat charming hut/stall, oversized stubby beams, thick rounded supports, broad cute awning with 3-4 large fabric sections, oversized simple jars and sacks. Compress fine architectural detail into memorable big shapes.
- Bridge and signs: fewer thick broad planks, short chunky posts and deliberately oversized readable silhouettes.
- Healing spring: compact round stone basin with fewer thick plump blocks and a simplified friendly decorative water spout, no realistically proportioned human statue. Clear aqua water shape.
- Flowers, mushrooms and ground tufts: enlarged charming shapes in small clusters rather than micro-detail everywhere. Sparse quiet markings in the open combat space.
Style: original bright 16-bit fantasy adventure, clearly deformed playful proportions but retain A's saturated adventurous palette, NOT pastel or painterly storybook. Authentic crisp coarse pixel art, deliberately hand-shaped low-resolution pixel clusters; think an effective 320-384 pixel-wide scene enlarged cleanly. Large stepped edges, compact purposeful shade ramps, dark contour accents, highlights, no smooth edges. Rich layered materials but substantially fewer little textures. No plain vector shapes, no airbrushed gradients, no realistic or semi-realistic architecture, no photorealism or 3D toy render.
The chibi character, trees, hut, stones, bridge and fountain must feel authored with ONE coherent squat, chunky, playful design language. Keep center spacious for action and 3-4 legible exits. Full opaque background. No extra characters, no new landmarks, no HUD, text, letters, captions, logos, watermark, frame, collage, or comparison inset. No blur, depth of field, or antialiasing.

refinements.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: FantasyRoyale art direction candidate A v004, restrained GBA-era fantasy pixel-art gameplay scene.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: v003 forest clearing. Input image 2 is a supporting MATERIAL / STYLE reference: v002, which has less cutesy outlines and more grounded adventurous timber and rock. Keep the geography and scene identity of image 1.
User correction: v003 is too cute. Aim for GBA-era top-down fantasy adventure pixel art: low-head-count sprite proportions and a stylized world, with confident heroic shapes and restrained charm rather than chibi baby proportions or toy-like rounded props.
Preserve A's bright yellow-green / emerald forest, turquoise water, ochre dirt, upper-left sunlight; center clearing, left stream and bridge, upper-right merchant stall, right healing spring, connecting routes, single ochre-caped blue-clothed adventurer. Landscape 3:2, near-overhead 2D gameplay view, no horizon. Same camera and map-scale composition.
Character correction: around 2.5 to 3 heads tall, compact classic handheld RPG sprite. Slightly oversized head but smaller relative to body than image 1. Clearly recognizable short torso, distinct short legs, readable arms and modest sword/shield. Small simple pixel eyes, understated calm determined expression, no giant sparkling eyes or round baby cheeks. Character remains low-head-count and compact, not an adult realistic figure. At this scene scale the hero is small, approximately the same height as the source. The pose feels like an adventurer ready to explore.
World correction — reduce the excessive cuteness everywhere, while retaining coarse stylization:
Trees have irregular somewhat pointed lobed foliage clusters with a few angular stepped tips, distinct dark/light leaf groupings, sturdier slightly taller trunks and visible tapered roots. They are stylized trees, not fluffy balls of plush leaves.
Rock ledges show a few broad angular facets, stepped cliff strata, warm mossy top and clear shadow faces. Replace pillow-like round rocks with faceted natural stones, keep readable irregular silhouette.
Merchant stall has practical squared timber framing, rectangular beams, modest cloth awning with a few small folds and slight wear, useful barrels and pottery. Reduce oversized balloon-like log columns and excessively swollen jars. Details remain economical, not elaborate realistic woodgrain.
Bridge posts and sign supports are squared, moderately sized and sturdily constructed. Keep broad readable planks, but remove toy-like round knobs.
Healing spring: mossy weathered stone basin with a small plain carved stone outlet. REMOVE the cute round face with big eyes entirely; replace it with an undecorated angular stone water spout. No animal faces or smiling props anywhere.
Ground flowers and mushrooms become smaller understated accents, less bright oversized decorative blooms. Keep cheerful classic fantasy colors but slightly reduce the neon saturation of the most extreme yellow-green patches, so the scene feels adventurous rather than sugary.
Pixel rendering: true crisp handheld-era coarse pixel art with deliberate larger clusters, economical material details, no micro-noise. Compact palette ramps and strong readable light/shadow grouping. Retain coarse pixel scale of v002 and v003, no return to high-detail v001. Think a low-resolution 384x256 scene cleanly enlarged to 1536x1024; this is an appearance guide, not a request for blurry pixelation. Original scene, no copying an existing game's character designs or map.
Visible priorities: moderated character head size; all-world GBA-like shape language; less rounded toy-like architecture; no face fountain; bright readable adventure atmosphere. Keep spacious movement and fighting paths. No added characters or landmarks, no text/HUD/labels/logo/watermark/frame/inset. No pastel storybook, no babyish kawaii, no modern mobile-game illustration, no photorealism or 3D, no smooth gradients, antialiasing, blur or depth of field.
